atomicity.reason: One obligation: replace the counted SoC with the open-circuit-voltage-derived value once the rest condition holds.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: trigger, action and purpose (bounding drift while cell voltages settle) are stated; 'counted state of charge' and 'open-circuit voltage' are standard domain terms.

feasibility.reason: OCV re-anchoring after a rest period is established practice and matches the linked corrector design; nothing contradicts it.

parent_fit.reason: Serves the parent's trust goal by bounding counting drift each time the pack rests, so the reported charge stays trustworthy beyond a single bench discharge.

unambiguity.reason: One reading: once absolute current has stayed below 1 A for at least 30 minutes the counted SoC is replaced by the OCV-derived one; threshold, duration and inclusive/exclusive limits are explicit.

verifiability.reason: The trigger is concrete (absolute pack current below 1 A continuously for at least 30 minutes) but the expected outcome is not: 'the value derived from the measured open-circuit voltage' names no OCV-to-SoC characteristic, no choice of measured voltage (cell mean, minimum, maximum) and no tolerance, so a test cannot say what SoC must be reported after the correction.
verifiability.suggestion: Reference the OCV-to-SoC characteristic and the voltage it is read at, and give an acceptance tolerance for the replaced value (or tie it to REQ_SOC_ACCURACY).

summary: Clear trigger and rationale; verifiability limited because the OCV-derived replacement value has no stated mapping or tolerance.
